cotonou.title: Cotonou
cotonou.intro: A coastal city best understood through its markets, street kitchens, music and the people who give each neighborhood its rhythm.
cotonou.heading: A city that moves by appetite.
cotonou.paragraph: Start at the market, follow the scent of charcoal and leave room for conversations. Cotonou reveals itself through small encounters as much as landmarks.

porto-novo.title: Porto-Novo
porto-novo.intro: A capital of layered histories, shaded streets, distinctive architecture and daily life that rewards an unhurried visit.
porto-novo.heading: Meet the city before breakfast.
porto-novo.paragraph: At first light, Ouando is already in conversation: baskets changing hands, zemidjans passing and breakfast ladled from enamel pots.
porto-novo.from: About 45 min from Cotonou; confirm current transport
porto-novo.note: Discover the city with a local

ganvie.title: Ganvié
ganvie.intro: A lakeside settlement where canoes are essential to everyday movement. Visit with respect for a living community, not as a spectacle.
ganvie.heading: Life follows the rhythm of water.
ganvie.paragraph: Come early, when the lake is stirring into the day. With a knowledgeable local guide, learn how water shapes work, trade, family life and food.
ganvie.from: Travel to the lakeside departure point, then continue by boat

ouidah.title: Ouidah
ouidah.intro: A place of memory, spiritual life, art and Atlantic coastline, where history remains present in streets, sites and ceremonies.
ouidah.heading: History still in motion.
ouidah.paragraph: Move slowly between memorial places, living cultural practices and the coast, making space for local voices and historical context.
ouidah.from: West of Cotonou; verify transport locally
ouidah.note: Approach sites and ceremonies with care

abomey.title: Abomey
abomey.intro: The historic heart of the Dahomey Kingdom, where royal memory, craft and contemporary life meet in a landscape of red earth.
abomey.heading: Memory in the red earth.
abomey.paragraph: Explore royal heritage with care, listening to the histories, objects and traditions that connect the past to the present.
abomey.from: Inland from the coast; plan transport ahead

grand-popo.title: Grand-Popo
grand-popo.intro: A coastal landscape where the Mono estuary, fishing communities and Atlantic shoreline shape the pace of the day.
grand-popo.heading: Where river meets sea.
grand-popo.paragraph: Follow the estuary with a local guide and learn how water, tides, work and meals are woven together.

natitingou.title: Natitingou
natitingou.intro: A gateway to northern landscapes, living traditions and communities of the Atacora region.
natitingou.heading: Take the red road north.
natitingou.paragraph: Go beyond the transit stop: make time for local guides, regional food and the landscapes that give the north its character.
natitingou.note: Seek local guidance for community visits

so-ava.title: Sô-Ava
so-ava.intro: Lakeside gateway to the water towns—pirogues, morning markets and the slow rhythm of Lake Nokoué.
so-ava.heading: Where the lake begins to speak.
so-ava.paragraph: Sô-Ava is less a spectacle than a working shore: embarkations, nets, and conversations that set the tone before you reach the stilt city.

pendjari.title: Pendjari
pendjari.intro: One of West Africa's last great wildlife reserves—elephants, lions and open savanna, approached with guides and time.
pendjari.heading: The north still holds wild ground.
pendjari.paragraph: Pendjari rewards patience: dry-season tracks, early drives, and the knowledge that this park is part of a wider cross-border ecosystem.

tanougou.title: Tanougou Falls
tanougou.intro: Cascades in a rock amphitheatre—a cool pause on the road to Pendjari and the northern hills.
tanougou.heading: Water in the hills.
tanougou.paragraph: Tanougou is a stop with intention: shade, sound of water, and a sense of the Atacora beyond the transit towns.

possotome.title: Possotomè
possotome.intro: A lakeside town on Ahémé known for thermal springs, calm water and a slower Mono rhythm—best approached without rush.
possotome.heading: Water that holds the day.
possotome.paragraph: Possotomè is not a checklist stop. Come for the lake edge, the springs, and the sense that Mono life organises itself around water, work and quiet hospitality.
possotome.note: Combine with Lake Ahémé and local guides

bopa.title: Bopa
bopa.intro: A working Mono town and gateway toward Lake Ahémé—markets, river life and the practical heart of the southwest.
bopa.heading: Gateway to the Mono waters.
bopa.paragraph: Bopa rewards attention to ordinary movement: stalls, transport junctions, and the people who keep the lake and road connected. Use it as a hinge, not only a transit name.
bopa.note: Useful base for Ahémé and Possotomè

allada.title: Allada
allada.intro: A historic kingdom seat and living town—where royal memory, markets and daily traffic share the same ground.
allada.heading: History under ordinary light.
allada.paragraph: Allada is not a museum. Royal lineages, market noise and road life sit side by side. Come ready to listen as much as to look.

parakou.title: Parakou
parakou.intro: The main urban hub of central-north Benin—rail memory, markets, and a crossroads between south and the Sahel edge.
parakou.heading: A city that turns the map.
parakou.paragraph: Parakou is where distances change. Markets, transport yards and regional kitchens make it a place to understand the country’s middle belt—not only pass through it.
parakou.note: Plan rest and local food stops

ketou.title: Kétou
ketou.intro: A historic Yoruba town of the Plateau—walls, memory and a cultural life that still shapes the southeast.
ketou.heading: A town that keeps its own time.
ketou.paragraph: Kétou holds layers of Yoruba history in a living town. Walk with attention: fortifications, market days and the quieter spaces where memory is not performed for visitors.
